title: Karl Organizing: Childcare Collectives
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Childcare Collectives] How can we support the parents in our organizing circle who can't find sitters?

Look, Build a childcare rotation where those of us without kids take shifts watching the little ones during meetings and actions. It's not 'babysitting'; it's revolutionary support that allows parents—especially moms—to lead the fight. Make sure there's a safe, fun space with snacks and activities so the kids actually want to be there. We raise the next generation of rebels together, as a village, not as isolated nuclear families.

title: Karl Organizing: Bail Funds
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Bail Funds] A friend asked me: 'What happens if someone in our network gets arrested?' What do I tell them?

You need to have a legal defense fund ready before the first person is taken. Chip in monthly to a community pot so you can post bond the second the window opens. Have a lawyer's number written in permanent marker on your arm before you go to any action. We don't leave comrades to rot in a cell just because they're broke; we pool our resources and bring everyone home. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Red Lines
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Red Lines] Can you explain: how do we know when a compromise is actually a sell-out?

If the deal helps the bosses more than the workers, or if it throws one part of your coalition under the bus to save the rest, it’s a sell-out. Never trade the rights of one group for a tiny raise for another; that’s how the ruling class divides us. A real win leaves your coalition stronger and more united for the next fight, not fractured and suspicious. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: internal Conflict
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: internal Conflict] Give me the short version: What do we do when two groups in the coalition start fighting each other?

Drag them back to the shared demand and remind them who the real enemy is. If the beef is personal, tell them to settle it on their own time because the warehouse workers or the tenants are waiting on us to lead. We aren't here to be a family; we are here to be a fist, and a fist doesn't work if the fingers are trying to snap each other.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: social Media OPSEC] Give me the short version: I want to post photos of the march to inspire people, is that okay?

Let me break it down: Inspiration is good, but snitching is better for the enemy. Before you post, use an app to scrub the metadata—that's the hidden digital tag that tells the feds exactly where and when the photo was taken. Blur every single face, including the background. If you don't have time to redact the identities of your comrades, keep that photo on your drive and out of the cloud.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, sliding Scales
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, sliding Scales] How do we implement a sliding scale for events?

Look, Be explicit about who each tier is for. Label the low end for students and the unemployed, the middle for workers, and the high end for 'solidarity' from those with a little extra cushion. It forces people to reflect on their own class position and ensures that the struggle remains accessible to the very people we're fighting for.

title: Karl Organizing: Membership Perks
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Membership Perks] Do we need to give donors gifts like tote bags or stickers?

Real talk: The best 'perk' you can give a comrade is a victory against the bosses. Don't waste money on trinkets that eat into your margins. Give them a vote in the organization, a seat at the strategy table, and the knowledge that they are part of a serious force for change; that's worth more than any canvas bag.

title: Karl Organizing: Phone Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Phone Hygiene] A friend asked me: 'What should I do if a cop tries to take my phone?' What do I tell them?

Lock it instantly. On most modern phones, hitting the power button five times or holding the volume and power buttons will trigger a lockdown that requires a passcode to reopen. Don't say a word, don't give up the code, and demand a lawyer. Your data is the collective memory of our movement; don't let them pillage it because you were too slow to hit the lock. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Handling Incumbents
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Handling Incumbents] Can you explain: my opponent has been in office for 20 years. How do I beat that?

Real talk: Use their longevity as an indictment of the status quo. If things are a mess after two decades of their leadership, why should anyone give them another four years? Focus on the stagnation and the cozy relationships they’ve built with the local elite over those years. Frame yourself as the fresh air and the voice of a new generation that refuses to accept the same old failures.

title: Karl Organizing: Donor Capture
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Donor Capture] A friend asked me: 'A wealthy businessman wants to give us a large sum but has some 'suggestions' on our messaging. Should we take it?' What do I tell them?

Real talk: Tell him to keep his blood money and his opinions. The second you let a fat cat dictate your slogans is the second you stop being a threat to his class. If he wants to help, he can drop the cash in the bucket and walk away with no strings attached; otherwise, he's just buying a leash to put on your movement.

title: Karl Organizing: Community Fridge Startup
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Community Fridge Startup] A friend asked me: 'How do I start a fridge in my neighborhood without it getting shut down immediately?' What do I tell them?

Find a local business owner or a comrade with a porch and an outdoor outlet who doesn't give a damn about city ordinances. Buy a used fridge, paint it with bright colors so it's impossible to ignore, and plug it in right on the sidewalk. Don't ask for permission from the state; just keep it clean and organized so the neighbors see it as a lifeline rather than an eyesore. When we feed each other, we prove the bosses are obsolete.

Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: phone Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: phone Hygiene] Give me the short version: What's the best way to back up my phone before an action?

Let me break it down: Back it up to a local hard drive at home, then encrypt that drive with a strong password. Turn off all auto-syncing to the cloud—Apple and Google will hand over your 'private' backups the moment the state asks. Once your backup is safe at home, wipe any sensitive messages or photos from the device you're carrying. Travel light and travel clean.

title: Karl Organizing: Tenant rights research
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Tenant rights research] How do I learn my tenant rights?

Start with your city's tenant union or legal aid — they have know-your-rights guides for your specific laws. Read your lease carefully; landlords count on you not reading it. Document every maintenance request in writing. Know your state's rules on security deposits, notice periods, and retaliation. Knowledge is leverage. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Merch Strategy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Merch Strategy] A friend asked me: 'What kind of merch actually makes money for the movement?' What do I tell them?

Forget the cheap plastic trinkets that end up in a landfill. Print bold, defiant designs on union-made shirts or screen-print patches that comrades can sew onto their own gear to show their colors. Sell items that serve a purpose, like heavy-duty water bottles or thick canvas bags, and make sure every cent above cost goes toward organizing the next action.

title: Karl Organizing: Donor Capture
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

title: Karl Organizing: Secure Document Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Secure Document Sharing] A friend asked me: 'Is email safe if I use a provider like Proton?' What do I tell them?

It's better than Gmail, but it's not a silver bullet. If you're emailing someone on a regular server, that message is exposed the second it leaves Proton's walls. For real security, keep the sensitive talk inside Signal or use PGP encryption if you're technical. Treat email like a postcard that a cop might read at any sorting facility. Keep it brief and keep it clean.

title: Karl Organizing: Transparent Treasuries
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Transparent Treasuries] How do we keep people from worrying about where the money goes?

Radical transparency is the only way to build real trust. Post a simple, plain-English breakdown of every dollar spent on a public board or in your newsletter every single month. When people see that their hard-earned cash is buying flyers and bail buttons instead of fancy dinners for leaders, they'll be lining up to chip in again.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, sustaining the Work
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, sustaining the Work] I'm exhausted and feel like I'm burning out. How do I keep going?

Take a damn break and let the rest of the collective carry the load for a while. Mutual aid isn't a solo performance; it's a relay race where we pass the baton when our legs get heavy. If you burn yourself out, you're no good to the movement or your neighbors, so go rest and recharge. We're in this for the long haul, and that means pacing ourselves so we can see the revolution through to the end.

title: Karl Organizing: Safe Zones
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Safe Zones] How do we make our neighborhood a 'no-go' zone for ICE?

Here's how it works: Get local businesses to display stickers stating they won't let feds in without a warrant and train their staff on what to say. Map out every alley and 'safe house' where neighbors can duck in if they're being followed. Run regular drills so everyone knows exactly where to go when the alert hits. We create safety by making our neighborhoods too organized for the state to operate in.

title: Karl Organizing: Metadata Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Metadata Awareness] A friend asked me: 'What is 'scrubbing' and how do I do it?' What do I tell them?

Scrubbing means stripping the hidden data—location, camera type, time—from your files. Use an app like 'ImagePipe' on Android or 'Metapho' on iOS before sharing any protest photos. For PDFs and docs, use the 'ExifTool' or simple online scrubbers. This prevents the state from using a 'cool photo' to pinpoint exactly where you stood at 2:00 PM. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Legal Rights Training
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Legal Rights Training] Can you explain: what's the most important thing to teach neighbors about their rights?

The most powerful words anyone can say are 'I am remaining silent and I want a lawyer.' Teach everyone that the police are allowed to lie to you, so you should never believe a word they say during an interrogation. Run 'Know Your Rights' workshops in living rooms and parks until every kid on the block knows how to handle a stop. Knowledge is the first line of defense against the precinct. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Debate Strategy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Debate Strategy] A friend asked me: 'How do I handle a debate with a 'moderate' incumbent?' What do I tell them?

Don't let them hide behind 'incremental change' or 'budgetary constraints.' Call out their failures directly: show the people the tent cities that grew on their watch and the luxury condos they approved while residents were priced out. Pivot every technical question back to the material reality of the voters. Be the only person on that stage who speaks like a human being rather than a walking press release.

title: Karl Organizing: Conflict Resolution
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Conflict Resolution] A friend asked me: 'Two people in our collective are fighting and it's stalling our work. What now?' What do I tell them?

Sit them down with a neutral mediator and remind them that our real enemy is the ruling class, not each other. Focus on the harm caused and how to make it right rather than looking for someone to blame or 'cancel.' If we can't solve problems within our own ranks, we'll never be able to build a world that works for everyone. Keep the focus on the mission: feeding and protecting our people.

title: Karl Organizing: Social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Social Media OPSEC] Should I make my accounts private?

Private accounts are a hurdle, not a wall. The platforms still own your data and will sell you out. If you’re an organizer, have a public-facing 'persona' for outreach and a completely locked-down, pseudonymous account for your real life. Use a different photo, a different name, and never link the two. Starve the algorithm of your real connections.

title: Karl Organizing: Signature Gathering
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Signature Gathering] A friend asked me: 'How do we get on the ballot without a massive paid staff?' What do I tell them?

You need a brigade of volunteers who believe in the cause enough to hit the pavement every single weekend. Set up at grocery stores, transit hubs, and public parks to meet people where they already are. Treat every signature as a conversation and a potential new recruit for the movement, not just a box to check. We don't need consultants when we have a disciplined crew of comrades who know how to ask a neighbor for two minutes of their time.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: secure Communication
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: secure Communication] Give me the short version: Are voice memos safer than typing?

Voice memos are worse. They're easier to identify with voice-recognition software and can't be easily searched or redacted. If you're on Signal, they're encrypted, but they still exist as a file that can be played back if your phone is seized. Type it out, keep it brief, and set it to disappear. Your voice is a biometric signature; don't give it away for free. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Cop watch
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Cop watch] How do I start a cop watch program?

Real talk: Get a team, get cameras, learn the law on filming police in your state. Patrol the areas where stops happen most. Film from a safe distance, announce you're recording, never interfere. Publish the footage — sunlight is the point. And train everyone on what to do if an officer turns on YOU.

title: Karl Organizing: Anti-Harassment Tactics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Anti-Harassment Tactics] A friend asked me: 'How do we deal with aggressive 'sidewalk counselors' at clinics?' What do I tell them?

Use umbrellas and banners to block their signs and keep them from filming patients' faces. Play loud, upbeat music to drown out their harassment so patients don't have to hear their vitriol. Don't try to win an argument with someone who thinks they're on a mission from god; just neutralize their tools. We are the wall between the vulnerable and the hateful.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: bail Fund Priorities
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: bail Fund Priorities] Give me the short version: Our bail fund is small. How do we decide who to get out of jail first?

Prioritize the comrades most at risk: trans folks, people with urgent medical needs, and parents who might lose their kids if they miss a day of work. We aren't here to play judge or jury; we're here to snatch our neighbors back from the state's kidnapping machine. Get those who are facing the longest pre-trial stretches out first so they can fight their cases from a position of strength. Every person we free is a middle finger to the carceral state.

title: Karl Organizing: Rejecting Corporate Cash
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Rejecting Corporate Cash] A friend asked me: 'A local real estate developer offered to sponsor our community garden. Take it?' What do I tell them?

Absolutely not. Those developers are the ones driving your neighbors out of their homes; taking their money is just helping them paint a smiley face on displacement. If they want to help the garden, they can stop hiking the rent. We'll fund our own soil and seeds through bake sales and tool-shares before we take a bribe from a landlord.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, financial Transparency
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, financial Transparency] How do we handle the money we raise together?

Let me break it down: Put one person from each major group in charge of a joint bank account and publish every single expense to the whole coalition. Nothing kills a movement faster than rumors about where the cash went, so be obsessed with being open. Use the funds to print flyers, pay for bail, and chip in for the gas it takes to get comrades to the front lines.

title: Karl Organizing: Courtroom Tactics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Courtroom Tactics] I have a hearing in housing court. How should I handle it?

Never go into that courtroom alone. Bring twenty of your union comrades to sit in the gallery so the judge knows the community is watching. If you don't have a lawyer, stick to the facts: bring photos of the damage, logs of your ignored requests, and proof of your escrowed rent. The goal is to show you aren't a 'deadbeat,' but a tenant demanding the basic rights the landlord has stolen. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, winter Survival
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, winter Survival] It's freezing outside and the shelters are full. What can our group do tonight?

Pool resources to buy high-quality sleeping bags, hand warmers, and wool blankets to distribute at the encampments right now. Set up a warming station with hot coffee and soup in a garage or a basement and let people know they won't be turned away. If you see someone in danger, don't wait for permission—break a lock on a vacant building if you have to. No one should freeze to death in a city full of heated, empty offices.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: direct Action Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: direct Action Support] Give me the short version: How do we fund things like strike pay or protest supplies?

Here's the thing: You have to build these reserves before the fire starts. Create a dedicated 'Strike and Action' fund that you contribute to during the quiet months. When the picket line goes up, you won't be scrambling for sandwich money; you'll already have the resources to keep the line strong for weeks if you have to.

title: Karl Organizing: Mapping Vulnerability
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Mapping Vulnerability] Can you explain: how do we know which parts of our town need the most defense?

Talk to your neighbors—especially the elderly, the undocumented, and the unhoused—and ask them where they feel the most heat from the state. Track where the cops hang out and where the most arrests happen to identify the high-risk zones. Defense isn't about where you feel comfortable; it's about being where the danger is greatest. Map the pain to find where the shield needs to be. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: building Trust
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: building Trust] Give me the short version: How do I get my neighbors to trust me with their safety?

Stop talking and start doing. Help people with their groceries, clean up the local park, and show up when someone's car breaks down. Trust isn't built in a meeting; it's built in the daily work of being a good neighbor. People won't call you during a raid if they don't know you're someone who keeps their word. Solidarity is a practice, not a slogan.

title: Karl Organizing: Membership Perks
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Membership Perks] Can you explain: do we need to give donors gifts like tote bags or stickers?

Look, The best 'perk' you can give a comrade is a victory against the bosses. Don't waste money on trinkets that eat into your margins. Give them a vote in the organization, a seat at the strategy table, and the knowledge that they are part of a serious force for change; that's worth more than any canvas bag.

title: Karl Organizing: Night Safety
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Night Safety] A friend asked me: 'How can we keep the neighborhood safe at night without more patrols?' What do I tell them?

Let me break it down: Organize 'walking school buses' or evening stroll groups so nobody has to walk alone if they don't want to. Fix broken streetlights ourselves or install motion-sensor lights in dim areas with the permission of the residents. Increasing positive foot traffic is the best way to discourage actual harm. We light up the dark with solidarity, not with police sirens.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: burner Devices
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: burner Devices] Give me the short version: How do I get a burner phone without looking suspicious?

Don't go to the shop next to your house, and for the love of the movement, pay with cash. Buy a cheap flip phone and a prepaid SIM at a big box store where you're just another face in the crowd. Never turn it on at your house or link it to your personal accounts. A burner is for the mission, not for checking your personal emails.

title: Karl Organizing: Reaching the Unorganized
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Reaching the Unorganized] How do we bring in people who aren't already part of a group?

Focus on the problems they talk about at the kitchen table, not the stuff you read in a theory book. If their water is brown or their rent is doubling, that is your entry point to show them that a coalition is the only way to fight back. People don't join 'movements'; they join people who are actually getting things done to improve their lives right now.

title: Karl Organizing: Surveillance Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Surveillance Awareness] What is a Stingray and should I be worried about it?

A Stingray is a fake cell tower the feds use to hijack your phone's signal and track your location. They use them to map out who is at a protest and who they're talking to. Put your phone in a Faraday bag or turn on Airplane Mode when you're near the action. If you don't need to coordinate in real-time, leave the tracking device at home. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Lockout Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Lockout Defense] I came home and the landlord changed the locks. What are my rights?

That is an illegal lockout, and it's time to get loud. Call the police—not because they're your friends, but because they are often required to tell the landlord to let you back in. If that fails, your union brothers and sisters should help you break back into your own home. Then, sue the landlord for every cent they have for the illegal displacement. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Location Services
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Location Services] A friend asked me: 'Should I keep my GPS on so my friends can find me in a crowd?' What do I tell them?

Turn that tracker off immediately. Every time your GPS pings, a billionaire’s server logs your exact coordinates, and the cops can buy that data with a simple request. Use a specific meeting point and a physical map instead. If you must use a map app, use Organic Maps or something that works offline. Don't let the enemy map your movements in real-time.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, long-term Planning
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, long-term Planning] How do we move from 'rent-to-rent' to a sustainable war chest?

Look, Stop thinking month-to-month and start building a permanent infrastructure. Invest in your own tools—printers, sound systems, even a physical headquarters if you can manage it—so you aren't constantly bleeding cash to outside vendors. A movement that owns its own means of communication and assembly is a movement that the bosses can't easily starve out.

title: Karl Organizing: Quiet Zones
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quiet Zones] Some people find protests overwhelming. How can we help them stay?

Set up a designated 'low-stim' area at the back of the march or at the rally site where people can take a breather away from the drums and megaphones. Have a couple of comrades stationed there with water and earplugs to help people ground themselves. Inclusion means making sure everyone, including neurodivergent comrades, has a way to contribute without hitting a breaking point. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: public Messaging
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: public Messaging] Give me the short version: How do we talk to the public so they actually care about our coalition?

Cut the academic jargon and speak directly to people's empty pockets and rising bills. Your message needs to be simple enough to fit on a cardboard sign and bold enough to make a landlord nervous. Use words that sound like a gut punch to the ruling class, not a sociology thesis; people want to know how you're going to help them win. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, tenant Union Ties
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, tenant Union Ties] Should my campaign be linked to the local tenant union?

Absolutely. The tenant union is the backbone of working-class power in the city. Their struggle is your struggle, and your campaign should be a vehicle for their demands. When you win, you’re not just a politician; you’re an extension of their movement inside the government. Use your platform to amplify their strikes and their demands for universal rent control and the right to counsel in eviction court.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: legal Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: legal Support] Give me the short version: How do we find lawyers who will help us for free?

Look for the National Lawyers Guild or local radical law collectives who prioritize movement work over big fat paychecks. Offer them office space or help with their own needs in exchange for 'Know Your Rights' trainings for the community. We need legal eagles who understand that the law is a tool for the powerful, but we can use it to shield our comrades. Never walk into a fight without knowing who you're going to call when the handcuffs come out.

title: Karl Organizing: Medical Information
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Medical Information] I have a medical condition; how do I handle that if I'm taken in?

Write your essential medical info and any necessary medications on your skin in permanent marker. If you're processed, demand to see a medic immediately and don't stop making noise until they address your needs. Have a buddy on the outside ready to bring your prescriptions to the precinct to ensure the pigs don't 'forget' your healthcare.

title: Karl Organizing: Direct action
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Direct action] What is a 'march on the boss'?

It's when the whole crew walks into the manager's office together to hand over a list of demands or your union petition. You don't send one representative; you all go. It shows the boss that they can't just bully one person into silence. Seeing the boss's face turn pale when fifty workers walk in at once is a massive boost to morale and proves who really runs the place.

title: Karl Organizing: Ballot Access Laws
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Ballot Access Laws] The state just passed new laws making it harder for independents to run. What now?

They’re changing the rules because they’re terrified of us. We treat their hurdles as a mobilization opportunity—turn the signature gathering into a massive rally and a public education campaign about their voter suppression. File the lawsuits if you have to, but focus on building a movement so large that their paperwork tricks can't stop the tide. We don't ask for permission to represent our people; we take it.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: night Safety
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: night Safety] Give me the short version: How can we keep the neighborhood safe at night without more patrols?

Here's the thing: Organize 'walking school buses' or evening stroll groups so nobody has to walk alone if they don't want to. Fix broken streetlights ourselves or install motion-sensor lights in dim areas with the permission of the residents. Increasing positive foot traffic is the best way to discourage actual harm. We light up the dark with solidarity, not with police sirens.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, clothing Swaps
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, clothing Swaps] We have a ton of donated clothes. How do we distribute them effectively?

Forget the 'sorting center' model; just set up some racks in a public park and let people take what they need for free. Organize them by size and type so it doesn't look like a pile of trash, and make sure the winter gear is front and center when the temperature drops. If you have leftovers, get them to the local shelters or encampments directly. Dignity means being able to pick out your own coat without someone watching over your shoulder.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: intervention Ethics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: intervention Ethics] Give me the short version: When should I actually step in if I see a cop harassing someone?

Assess the situation and ask the person being harassed if they want help before you dive in. If they say yes, start filming and ask the officer for their name and badge number while standing at a safe distance. Sometimes just having three or four people watching silently with phones out is enough to make a bully in uniform back off. Solidarity means following the lead of the person in the crosshairs. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: anti-Harassment Tactics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: anti-Harassment Tactics] Give me the short version: How do we deal with aggressive 'sidewalk counselors' at clinics?

Use umbrellas and banners to block their signs and keep them from filming patients' faces. Play loud, upbeat music to drown out their harassment so patients don't have to hear their vitriol. Don't try to win an argument with someone who thinks they're on a mission from god; just neutralize their tools. We are the wall between the vulnerable and the hateful. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Inclusivity in Action
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Inclusivity in Action] A friend asked me: 'How do we make sure our coalition isn't just one type of person?' What do I tell them?

Go to where the people are instead of waiting for them to find your meeting in a basement. If you want immigrant workers in your coalition, you need translators and you need to show up for their fights before you ask them to show up for yours. Solidary isn't a feeling you get; it's a practice of showing up for people who the system tries to make invisible.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, secure Document Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, secure Document Sharing] Is email safe if I use a provider like Proton?

Here's how it works: It's better than Gmail, but it's not a silver bullet. If you're emailing someone on a regular server, that message is exposed the second it leaves Proton's walls. For real security, keep the sensitive talk inside Signal or use PGP encryption if you're technical. Treat email like a postcard that a cop might read at any sorting facility. Keep it brief and keep it clean.
